title: Peerie Faroese shawl
subtitle: A Faroese-shaped DK shawl with bands of traditional Shetland peerie patterns.
excerpt: A Faroese-shaped shawl in DK wool with alternating bands of three different Shetland peerie patterns worked throughout the garter field. Each peerie band is 4 rows tall; garter rows separate the bands across the full wingspan. Wingspan approximately 150 cm. About 300 g of main colour plus 100 g of contrast.
sourceNotes: Peerie patterns are small Shetland stranded motifs documented in Mary Thomas's Knitting Book (1938), §Colour Patterns, and in Sarah Don, The Art of Shetland Lace (1980), §Shetland Tradition. Three standard 8-stitch peerie motifs are used here: cross stitch, zigzag, and chevron. All are standard public domain Shetland motifs.

knitting.gaugeText: 22 sts × 44 rows = 10 × 10 cm in garter stitch on 4 mm needles, blocked.
knitting.finishedSizeText: Wingspan approximately 150 cm. Total depth approximately 72 cm. Blocked.

glossaryTerms.definition: A small stranded-colourwork motif of 6 to 12 stitches wide, used in Shetland knitting as a border or accent band. The word peerie is Shetland dialect for small. Each motif runs for 2 to 4 rows.
A shawl construction with five sections — two wings, two shoulder gussets, and a centre back — creating a curved shoulder fit. Increases run in the wings; decreases in the gussets.

content.text: bands in three Shetland motifs throughout the garter field. Wingspan approximately 150 cm.

The three peerie patterns, cross stitch (4 rows), zigzag (4 rows), and chevron (4 rows), cycle every 12 rows throughout the wings and centre back. The Faroese shoulder gussets are worked in MC garter only to keep the colourwork floats away from the shoulder shaping. Budget about 300 g of MC and 100 g of CC in DK wool.

content.text: 22 stitches and 44 rows to 10 cm over garter stitch on 4 mm needles, blocked. The peerie bands run approximately 2 stitches per 10 cm tighter than garter stitch due to float tension; the shawl will be slightly narrower in the colourwork rows but the difference averages out across the full wingspan.

Cast on 81 stitches. Place 4 section markers: left wing (6), left gusset (15), centre back (39), right gusset (15), right wing (6). Work the first 20 rows in MC garter stitch only, including all gusset shaping (gusset decreases, wing increases). After the gussets are complete (approximately 7 RS rows), introduce peerie bands.
Rows 1 to 4 (cross stitch peerie, 8 sts): RS Row 1: *k3 MC, k2 CC, k3 MC; repeat from *. RS Row 3: *k1 MC, k2 CC, k2 MC, k2 CC, k1 MC; repeat from *. WS rows: k all in respective colour.
Rows 5 to 8 (zigzag, 8 sts): RS Row 5: *k4 MC, k1 CC, k3 MC; repeat from *. RS Row 7: *k3 MC, k1 CC, k4 MC; repeat from *.
Rows 9 to 12 (chevron, 8 sts): RS Row 9: *k1 CC, k6 MC, k1 CC; repeat from *. RS Row 11: *k2 CC, k4 MC, k2 CC; repeat from *.

Between each 4-row peerie band, work 2 plain RS/WS garter rows in MC before starting the next band. Continue the Faroese wing increases throughout. Continue cycling peerie bands until wingspan reaches 150 cm.
Work Jeny's surprisingly stretchy bind-off in MC after a plain garter RS row.

Peerie bands pulled in at float lengths: the CC float spans 3 to 6 stitches in some rows. At 6 stitches the float is on the edge of what is comfortable for a garment; spread the stitches before crossing the float.

Peerie band alignment breaking at the wing increase positions: the two yarn-over increases on each RS row add stitches mid-row that shift the 8-stitch repeat alignment. After each wing increase RS row, re-count the stitches from the nearest marker to re-set the repeat start.
Wet-block to wingspan 150 cm and total depth 72 cm. Check for CC dye bleed before blocking.
Hand wash gently in cool water, lay flat to dry. Avoid agitating the WS floats.
Substitute a larger 12-stitch OXO peerie for one of the 8-stitch bands at a point where the wing is wide enough to carry the repeat.
